architecture.approach: A second pass over the existing chat module rather than a new slice. The seeded team channel is renamed to 'Project Chat' while its kind stays 'team', and the rename is applied to existing workspaces by extending the seeding pass that already runs on every channel list request, so no migration step is introduced. A task assignment keeps using addAssigneesToProjectMembers as the single membership hook, which grows a return value of the ids it actually added; callers ensure the project channel exists and emit one chat:channel-granted per (project, user) to the assignee's user room, and the client appends, dedupes and joins the room. Attachments stop being anchors to a protected route and are fetched as blobs through the authenticated axios client into a refcounted object-URL cache, rendered as thumbnails or file cards and opened in an in-app lightbox. Pasted code becomes a fenced block and renders through a new code card whose highlighter is a lazy chunk with a plain-monospace fallback. The project detail header gains an Open chat action backed by a get-or-create project-channel endpoint, and the chat header's empty member handler becomes a panel fed by a channel-scoped member endpoint resolved in two queries. Message payloads carry a populated author on every emit, with a client-side directory fallback so a known participant is never rendered as 'Unknown member'.

dataModel.flowDescription: assignee -> addAssigneesToProjectMembers returns the newly added ids -> createProjectChannel ensures the project channel exists -> chatGrant collapses the pairs -> emitToUser('chat:channel-granted', channelCard) -> client appends, dedupes and joins the channel room. Separately: MessageItem -> AttachmentCard -> useAttachmentUrl -> axios blob fetch with the bearer token -> cached object URL -> thumbnail or lightbox, revoked on last unmount. And: project detail header -> GET /chat/projects/:projectId/channel (get-or-create) -> navigate to /{workspaceSlug}/chat/{channelId}. Amendment flow (2026-10-28): the sidebar's Project chat item links to the chat root, which renders the merged conversation list with nothing selected, ordered by mergeConversations plus sortConversations with the header outside the message scroll container; an attachment is fetched through AttachmentCard and the route now passes the caller's project membership into decideChannelAccess; a reply persists, increments the parent and emits chat:thread with the authoritative count, and the client patches that parent row and appends the reply to an open thread panel.

securityConsiderations.description: Both new routes run protect then requirePermission('chat:read') and resolve the channel with the v1 loadChannelForCaller rules; a non-member receives 404 for a project channel, so project existence is not leaked.
projectId and channelId pass through an express-validator isMongoId chain, and every query filters by req.workspace._id with no user input interpolated into a query.
Code and message bodies render as React text nodes; dangerouslySetInnerHTML is not introduced, and the highlighter emits token elements rather than HTML strings.
New routes inherit Helmet, the general rate limiter and the shared error handler; no bypass and no direct process.env read is added.
Attachment bytes travel through the authenticated axios client over HTTPS; no token in a URL or query string, no long-lived public link, no new storage service.
The upload MIME allow-list and filename sanitisation remain the only content gate; a stored image/* type is a rendering hint and a decode failure falls back to the file card.

The attachment route resolves project membership for a project channel and still answers 404 for a caller who may not read the message's channel (direct, project or unknown alike), so no existence information leaks; no token is placed in a URL and the blob fetch keeps using the authenticated axios client.

performanceConsiderations.strategy: The grant rides the existing user room: one $addToSet diff and one upsert per granted project, so the 2-second p95 budget is met by the socket path with no added polling.
The channel member endpoint resolves the audience and the distinct role ids in two queries regardless of member count; no per-member lookup.
One object URL per attachment id for the life of the message list, refcounted and revoked on last unmount; only rendered messages are fetched.
The highlighter is a lazy chunk and snippets above 20,000 characters render as plain monospace, so first paint and typing are unaffected.
The code card scrolls its own horizontal overflow and the panel is a full-height sheet at 320px, so the conversation never widens.

Bounding the chat screen is a static layout change (a route-scoped height on the inset plus min-h-0 at every flex level): no resize observer, no virtualisation, and the message page size is untouched.

A reply emits one four-field summary to the channel room the member is already in, replacing a client-side guess, so the parent row updates without a refetch and the count stays authoritative after a reload.

Unread reconciliation compares the stored read timestamp with the channel's activity and writes at most one read state per conversation open; the sidebar patches rows from the events it already receives instead of re-fetching, and no polling interval is added.
Clearing a badge and raising the sender's card are local state patches over data already loaded: no extra request, no polling, and the existing single markRead write is unchanged.

risks.description: RISK-007: feature/chat is about 100 commits behind main, so the eventual merge conflicts in the chat files.
risks.mitigation: Confine edits to the files named in the plan and treat the merge as a separate reviewed step.

risks.description: RISK-008: the syntax highlighter can add bundle weight.
risks.mitigation: Lazy import, a small language set and the 20,000-character cap.

risks.description: RISK-009: caching image blobs can grow memory in a long session.
risks.mitigation: One cache entry per attachment id, revoked on last unmount, only rendered messages fetched.

risks.description: RISK-010: a bulk assignment could emit many channel events.
risks.mitigation: Diff the member list and collapse events by project and user before emitting.

risks.description: RISK-011: renaming the stored channel can collide with an existing 'Project Chat' row under the unique (workspace, kind, nameKey) index.
risks.mitigation: Rename only when no team row already holds the target name; otherwise leave the existing row untouched.

risks.description: RISK-012: changing the message renderer can regress the v1 search jump, pin panel or thread panel.
risks.mitigation: Keep the body renderer a child component and preserve the data-message-id contract used by search.

risks.description: RISK-013: a bounded height can clip content on a short viewport, at 200% zoom or with the software keyboard open.
risks.mitigation: min-h-0 at every flex level, the composer outside the scroll container, and a browser check at 320x568 and 200% zoom.

risks.description: RISK-014: the sidebar item removes the desktop shortcut to the seeded team channel.
risks.mitigation: The channel stays a row in the merged list with its unread state, and the browser pass confirms it is reachable.

risks.description: RISK-015: the chat root no longer redirects, so older links land on the list.
risks.mitigation: The root shows the list with an explicit empty pane, the conversation route is unchanged, and the README update is a documentation task.

risks.description: RISK-016: a patched reply count can drift if an event is missed while the socket is disconnected.
risks.mitigation: listMessages re-derives the count on the next load and the thread event carries the authoritative value rather than a delta.

risks.description: RISK-017: one merged list changes a surface that AC-056 and AC-065 fixed.
risks.mitigation: The row rendering is extracted rather than rewritten, so previews, badges and the picker position are preserved, and the spec records the amendment explicitly.

risks.description: RISK-018: a fixed dark scrim can swallow the dialog's own controls in the light theme.
risks.mitigation: Keep the title, close and download controls on the inverse tokens and re-check their contrast in both themes.

risks.description: RISK-019: patching the sender's card optimistically can disagree with the server's order when clocks differ.
risks.mitigation: Use the timestamp in the server response for the card and let the next list load replace the local value.
